body.text: Stage 1 began at 2026-11-02T21:54:44Z with a 60-minute deadline. Reconstruct the actual right hand using HaWoR then the supplied MANO fitter. Treat longitudinal pen roll as unobservable; distinguish video evidence from the four-half-turn sequence specified by TASK.md. No training simulation has been built.

The baseline reconstruction has pen-mask IoU 0.803 and hand precision 0.826, but FCL reports distal finger intersections on 81.7% of frames. Image agreement is insufficient. Refining a writable workspace copy of the supplied fitter with an explicit distal capsule separation term; default fit and all failed checks are preserved.

body.summary: 180-frame pen and right-hand reconstruction. check_reference VALID; physical validation pass with retained thumb-opposition warning. Net directed image-plane motion 711.8 degrees clockwise. Camera depth and exact support pairs remain uncertain.

components.name: camera
components.method: MoGe median focal prior; background-boundary roll; inferred gravity plane
components.note: Focal not independently identifiable; camera translation/pitch/yaw unresolved.

components.name: object 6D motion
components.method: SAM3 elongated masks, endpoints and ring heading, known-length perspective lift
components.note: 180 uncertain estimates, net clockwise heading 711.8 degrees; axial roll unobservable.

components.name: hand motion
components.method: HaWoR then default MANO fit and documented local self-collision refinement
components.note: 180/180 valid; mean fitted mask IoU .8113; zero FCL intersections; estimates not ground truth.

components.name: contact phases
components.method: Visual scene analysis and closest-finger checks
components.note: Nearest-finger distance passes; exact instructed pair order remains inferred; thumb-opposition warning retained.

limitations: Axial pen roll unobservable; stored roll is a gauge.
Focal length, gravity direction and metric depth use explicit priors; camera translation is unresolved.
Exact finger-pair order is partly instruction-derived; nearest-finger distance does not prove two-finger support.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

body.reason: Before RL evaluation, require pair dominance so a constant multi-finger cage cannot satisfy the instructed transfer order. Initial geometric grasp tests revealed incidental ring contact; no trained policy has yet been evaluated.

simulator.name: MuJoCo
simulator.solver: Newton 40 iterations, tolerance 1e-9, elliptic friction cone, implicitfast
simulator.contact: rigid convex pieces; solref .006–.008s, solimp .95 .99 .001; sliding friction .6–.9 random, torsional .005, rolling .0001

scene.hand: public right URDF and meshes, all masses preserved, free root
scene.pen: Blender-exported convex profile pieces and blue/red/white/yellow/green visual meshes, exact specified mass/inertia

reference.method: Anatomical wrist frame from wrist/MCP joints, thumbward +X, palm +Y, distal -Z. World axes/gravity preserved, origin shifted to initial wrist at (0,0,.45). Five-finger bounded IK tracks bone directions; offline initialization adjusts pen position 27 mm and four MCP joints to establish the demonstrated starting gap. Initial joint offset decays with 15-frame constant. Object/axis and wrist tracks guide rewards; reference replay alone is only a baseline.

wrist_and_fingers.controller: hardware/SPECS.md wrist-1 and finger PD at 1kHz; policy 500Hz held2ticks; own-weight compensation M=.6878; force/torque norm limits30N/2Nm; speed limits1m/s,3rad/s
wrist_and_fingers.finger_efforts: joint-specific saturation, armatures vendor values; positions clipped for targets; actual speed/position violations terminate and fail
wrist_and_fingers.policy_sensors: privileged simulated object pose and velocity, joint encoders, wrist state, reference, previous actions and time; no tactile/contact inputs
wrist_and_fingers.policy_residuals: Finger offsets +/-0.6rad; wrist offsets +/-0.03m and +/-0.2rad around reconstructed trajectory. This policy parameterization is not an environmental workspace constraint.

initial_conditions.reason: Reconstructed start retargeted to morphology, then geometric fit of index/middle contact. No fixtures or object constraints.
initial_conditions.randomization: q +/- .01rad, pen xyz +/-2mm, heading +/-3deg; uniform friction .6–.9

episode.termination: horizon, dropped/floor pen or any finger hardware violation

validation.initial_hold: untrained zero-residual reference controller retains pen for2s, obeys hardware; this is not the final learned policy
validation.baseline_full_skill: controller_validation_rate_limited.json records that replay is insufficient; not a task-success result
validation.limitations: Convex hand geometry, rigid pads, uncertain friction and monocular depth; no real-world transfer claim.

body.text: Simulation v1 is now recorded as r0006. Its first upload failed because .gz attachments are unsupported, and its next upload lacked the required reconstruction_version field. An inadvertently launched trainer ran 129024 hold-curriculum steps before I noticed; it was interrupted, preserved under research/aborted_before_sim_record, and will not be resumed or evaluated. The new PPO run starts from fresh seed7 weights after r0006. Assets are attached as a genuine NumPy archive of named byte arrays, not a renamed tar file.

Final-policy design: a closed-loop actor/critic network trained with clipped PPO (Schulman et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347). The actor sees noisy joint encoders, wrist state, privileged simulated pen pose/velocity, reference targets, previous actions and phase; it outputs 26 bounded residual commands. The retargeted trajectory is an allowed base controller under LEARNING.md, not the reported policy by itself. No execution-time optimizer, pen attachment or object-pose force is used. Criteria v2 additionally requires pair dominance to exclude a constant multi-finger cage.

Iteration1 training return and survival improve, but accepted pair stages remain zero in the running curves. Two likely causes need testing: wrist exploration is too large for 500Hz impedance control, and the initial robot-specific grasp correction decays before the demonstrated first transfer. Next candidate: smaller wrist action variance and retain the initial correction through the first hold, then taper it during transfer. These are hypotheses, not verified task progress.
